description:
Hit in examples/hashes.exs (defk-9p6.20): an 8 KB binary attribute (`@t <<...>>`) read with `u32_le(@t, ...)` inside a helper kernel called 8 times from one kernel appears 9 times in the generated C, once per inlined use site, as a fresh string literal. Repro: `@t <<...8 KB...>>`, `defk f(k :: i64, x :: i64) :: i64, do: u32_le(@t, ...)`, called 8x in one kernel; count the literal in `__defk_source__/0`. Emit each binary attribute (and each binary literal, defk-n4r.5, which shares `static_u8/1`) once per module as a `static const uint8_t` array named by a hash of its contents, and reference it from every use site. Clang may merge identical literals anyway, but the C file size and compile time grow (defk-6ag). Also noted there: indexing into the table goes through checked `defk_mul_i64`/`defk_bsl_i64`; see defk-upc (range facts for constant multiples).

Done when: a repeated attribute or literal appears once in the generated C (test on `__defk_source__`), and the examples' generated C shrinks accordingly (record the before/after size for hashes.exs).

comments.text: Generated C of examples/hashes.exs kernels module (Hashes.CRC32CTables + Hashes.Kernels), byte_size(__defk_source__()): before 2,115,100 bytes, after 326,375 bytes (-85%). Each binary attribute/literal is now one static const uint8_t defk_lit_<sha256-prefix>[] declared before all functions.

title: A binary attribute is emitted as a fresh string literal at every inlined use site
